# dsh-model-caps

Fetch a provider's real `/models` list, review the capability fields it exposes
(context window, max

output, image input), edit them on one page, then save them
back into `llm-pi-ai`.

Unlike catalog lookups that match a model **name** against a static table, this
plugin asks the conf

igured upstream and shows only what the upstream actually
returned. Missing fields stay blank instea

d of being guessed, and vision support
can be proven by a real image probe.
## Why

`llm-pi-ai` accepts `contextWindow`, `maxTokens` and `input` per model, but most
OpenAI-compatible g

ateways return only an id from `GET /models`. Filling those
fields by hand is error-prone, and name-

based catalogs are wrong for private
routes. This plugin keeps a human in the loop: fetch, inspect,

ogs are wrong for private
routes. This plugin keeps a human in the loop: fetch, inspect, edit, save.
## Install

Then restart the profile, or let `dsh-hotswap` mount it when it is already
installed.
## Use

1. Open `http://127.0.0.1:3080/model-caps/` in the same browser session as the
Web UI (the cookie au

thenticates the page).
2. Pick a provider. The list comes from `llm-pi-ai.providers`.
3. Click **Fet

ch upstream**. The plugin calls `GET {baseURL}/models` with that
provider's key from `apiKeyEnv` ->

the credential store.
4. Review the table. Fields sourced from the upstream payload are marked in th

e
notes column; blank means the upstream did not expose it.
5. Optionally select rows and click **Pr

obe vision**: a 32x32 red/blue PNG is
sent and a model counts as image-capable only when it answers

with a colour.
6. Edit any cell, then click **Save**. The plugin writes
`llm-pi-ai.providers.<id>.mo

dels` through `settings.mutate`, preserving
fields it did not touch.
## Page file\n\nThe editor UI lives in `dsh/model-caps.html` and is read from disk on every request,

so a UI change takes effect on refresh without restarting DSH.

## Editor

The editor is a stan
dalone page at `/model-caps/`, served from `dsh/model-caps.html` and read from disk on every request
, so UI edits apply on refresh without restarting DSH. It is paginated (80 rows per page) and filter
s are debounced, so a 50+ model provider stays responsive.\n\n## Endpoints
| Method | Path | Purpose |

| GET | `/model-caps/` | The editor page |
| GET | `/model-caps/providers` | Configured providers, `

apiKeyEnv`, model counts |
| POST | `/model-caps/fetch` | `{ provider }` -> upstream rows merged wit

h current config |
| POST | `/model-caps/vision` | `{ provider, ids }` -> per-model image support |
| POST | `/model-caps/save` | `{ provider, rows }` -> write the model list back |
## Parsed capability fields
The reader accepts the common spellings gateways use:

- context: `context_length`, `context_window`, `max_context_length`,
`max_input_tokens`, `max_model_

len`, `top_provider.context_length`,
`limits.context`
- output: `max_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `

max_completion_tokens`,
`top_provider.max_completion_tokens`, `limits.output`
- image input: `archit

ecture.input_modalities`, `input_modalities`,
`modalities.input`, `capabilities.vision`, `supports_v

alities`, `input_modalities`,
`modalities.input`, `capabilities.vision`, `supports_vision`, `vision`
## Safety

- The page and endpoints live behind the same authentication fence as the Web
UI; a request without

a valid session is rejected.
- The upstream is only contacted for the provider you select, and only

when you
press a button.
- Saving replaces the model list of that one provider. Entries that were no

t on
the upstream are shown marked and are dropped unless you keep them.
- The API key never leaves

the host: the browser talks to DSH, DSH talks to the
provider.
